title: Year 11 Chemistry Module 3 – Reactive Chemistry
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 11 Chemistry Module 3. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What type of reaction joins two or more substances to form one product?
What type of reaction breaks one compound into simpler substances?
What gas is required for a combustion reaction?
What insoluble solid forms when some aqueous ionic solutions react?
What three products usually form when an acid reacts with a carbonate?
questions.answer: A salt, carbon dioxide and water.

questions.prompt: What ion is produced by acids in aqueous solution?
What ion is associated with alkaline aqueous solutions?
What reaction occurs when an acid reacts with a base?
What two products usually form in an acid–base neutralisation reaction?
What equation shows only the reacting ions and omits spectator ions?
questions.answer: A net ionic equation. Accept: ionic equation.

questions.prompt: What list ranks metals from most reactive to least reactive?
questions.answer: The activity series. Accept: reactivity series.

questions.prompt: What gas commonly forms when a reactive metal reacts with dilute acid?
What type of reaction occurs when a more reactive metal replaces a less reactive metal ion in solution?
Which is generally easier to oxidise: a more reactive metal or a less reactive metal?
What term describes the gradual reaction of a metal with its environment, such as rusting?
What process involves loss of electrons?
What process involves gain of electrons?
What reaction involves both oxidation and reduction?
What device converts chemical energy into electrical energy using a spontaneous redox reaction?
questions.answer: A galvanic cell. Accept: voltaic cell.

questions.prompt: At which electrode does oxidation occur in a galvanic cell?
What theory explains reaction rates using collisions between particles?
What minimum energy must colliding particles have for a reaction to occur?
Increasing temperature generally makes a chemical reaction faster or slower?
Increasing the surface area of a solid reactant generally makes a reaction faster or slower?
What substance speeds up a reaction without being consumed overall?

finalRound.prompt: In a redox reaction, which process is defined as the loss of electrons?
